d-l2-3bet-q1.question: MP open(2.5BB), you hold AsQs in CO — how should you 3-Bet?
d-l2-3bet-q1.explanation: AsQs vs an MP open is a strong 3-Bet candidate. It blocks AA/KK/AK — the standard size is about 3x the open+ (7.5-8BB).

d-l2-3bet-q2.question: MP open(2.5BB), CO 3-Bets to 8BB, hero in BB holds AJs — call or fold?
d-l2-3bet-q2.explanation: AJs in BB vs a CO 3-Bet has a positional advantage (IP postflop) — calling is standard. Enough implied odds and AJs plays well postflop.

d-l2-3bet-q3.question: CO open(2.5BB), you hold AK on the BTN — what should you do?
d-l2-3bet-q3.explanation: AK on the BTN vs a CO open is a standard 3-Bet. With positional advantage, AK is a premium value 3-Bet. The IP 3-Bet size is 7.5-8BB (about 3-3.2x).

d-l2-3bet-q4.question: BTN open(2.5BB), you hold 76s in SB — what should you do?
d-l2-3bet-q4.explanation: 76s in SB vs BTN is a classic 3-Bet bluff candidate. It has a positional disadvantage but good postflop playability — the 3-Bet captures fold equity. The OOP 3-Bet size is 9-10BB (about 3.5-4x).

d-l2-3bet-q5.question: UTG open(2.5BB), you hold AJ suited in CO — what should you do?
d-l2-3bet-q5.explanation: Against the strong UTG open range, AJ in CO is too weak. The UTG range is strong (TT+, AQs+, AK) — AJ is easily dominated.

d-l2-3bet-q6.question: MP open(2.5BB), you hold AJs on the BTN — what should you do?
d-l2-3bet-q6.explanation: AJs on the BTN vs MP has positional advantage — calling is the best choice. A 3-Bet is also possible, but calling better exploits position postflop.

d-l2-3bet-q7.question: UTG open(2.5BB), you hold QQ in MP — what should you do?
d-l2-3bet-q7.explanation: QQ is a premium hand — 3-Bet for value against a UTG open. Don't slowplay QQ and let too many hands see the flop. The IP 3-Bet size is 7.5-8BB (about 3-3.2x).

d-l2-3bet-q8.question: CO open(2.5BB), you hold 54s on the BTN — what should you do?
d-l2-3bet-q8.explanation: 54s on the BTN vs CO has a great position — calling uses position and implied odds correctly. Suited connectors play strongly postflop.

d-l2-pos-q1.question: You hold JTs in UTG — what should you do?
d-l2-pos-q1.explanation: JTs in UTG is at the edge of the open range. UTG opens only the very strongest slice of hands — JTs just makes the cut.

d-l2-pos-q2.question: You hold K9s in UTG — what should you do?
d-l2-pos-q2.explanation: K9s in UTG is too weak — not in the open range. UTG needs the strongest hands; K9s is easily dominated.

d-l2-pos-q3.question: Everyone folds to you on the BTN with ATs — what should you do?
d-l2-pos-q3.explanation: ATs on the BTN is an easy open. The BTN is the widest opening position at a 6-max table (about 35%) — ATs is well within range.

d-l2-pos-q4.question: Everyone folds to you on the BTN with 87o — what should you do?
d-l2-pos-q4.explanation: 87o on the BTN is too weak — not in the open range. Even on the BTN, small offsuit hands aren't worth opening. 87s yes, but 87o no.

d-l2-pos-q5.question: Everyone folds to you in CO with Q9s — what should you do?
d-l2-pos-q5.explanation: Q9s in CO is a standard open. The CO widens noticeably (nearly 30%) — Q9s is in range.

d-l2-pos-q6.question: Everyone folds to the SB, you hold T8s — what should you do?
d-l2-pos-q6.explanation: SB vs BB should use raise-or-fold. T8s is strong enough to open with the standard 2.5-3BB size.

d-l2-pos-q7.question: Everyone folds to you on the BTN with 72o — what should you do?
d-l2-pos-q7.explanation: 72o is the weakest starting hand — fold from any position. Even the wide BTN range excludes this garbage.

d-l2-pos-q8.question: Everyone folds to you in MP with A5s — what should you do?
d-l2-pos-q8.explanation: A5s in MP is a standard open. Suited Ax has great blocking effects and postflop playability — in the MP open range.

l2-raise-sizing: In online 6-max cash games, the standard preflop raise size is 2.5BB (2.5 times the big blind). For example, at $1/$2 the standard raise is $5.
Never use different raise sizes that expose your hand strength. Whether you hold AA or 76s, you should raise the same size.

Bigger raise → bigger pot → higher opponent fold rate → your range should be stronger
Smaller raise → smaller pot → higher opponent call rate → you can use a wider range
Pro players use a uniform raise size to hide information. If you raise $8 with strong hands and $5 with weak hands, opponents will quickly spot your pattern.

Pot-odds formula derivation:
Required equity = call amount ÷ (current pot + opponent bet + call amount)

Example: pot 100, opponent bets 50 → required equity = 50÷(100+50+50) = 25%

Required equity by common bet size:
1/3 pot bet → 20%
1/2 pot bet → 25%
2/3 pot bet → 28.6%
Full pot bet → 33.3%

Theory reference: the complete definition and derivation of pot odds is in Theory Academy T2 Chapter 2 "Pot Odds: The Price Tag of a Call", including the required-equity formula derivation from the EV=0 break-even point.

Counter-intuitive: the bigger your raise, the more opponents fold — but your success rate isn't necessarily higher. A larger raise makes calling more expensive, but it also risks more to win a limited pot. 2.5BB is the optimized balance point.
l2-3bet-basics: A 3-Bet is a re-raise against an open raise preflop. The "3" comes from the blinds counting as the first bet, the open raise as the second, and the re-raise as the third.

1. Value: build a big pot with strong hands (AA/KK/QQ/AKs)
2. Fold equity: force folds and win the pot directly
3. Initiative: take control of postflop betting (initiative)
4. Isolation: play heads-up against a specific opponent, avoiding multiway pots
Beginners should start with a "linear 3-Bet range" (3-Betting only strong hands), then add a "polarized 3-Bet range" (strong hands + some weak hands as bluffs) once comfortable.
3-Bet frequency is a key indicator of aggression. Being too passive (rarely 3-Betting) loses value; being too aggressive lets opponents exploit you.

3Bet range combinatorics:
Opponent 3Bet range = {AA, KK, QQ, AKs, A5s}
AA = 6, KK = 6, QQ = 6, AKs = 4, A5s = 4
Total = 26 combinations

Blocker effect: when you hold A♠,
AA drops from 6 to 3, AKs from 4 to 3
The 3Bet range drops from 26 to 22

Theory reference: 3Bet range construction and combinatorics are detailed in Theory Academy T4 Chapter 2 "Combinatorics and Blockers", with a full derivation of Blocker applications in preflop 3Bet/4Bet spots.

Counter-intuitive: when you 3-Bet holding A5s, AA drops from 6 to 3 combinations (blocked by your A), but the K count is completely unaffected. That means holding A5s halves the probability your opponent has AA — the mathematical basis for 3-Bet bluffing with A5s.
l2-4bet-strategy: A 4-Bet is the re-raise against a 3-Bet. Preflop betting sequence: blinds (1) → Open (2) → 3-Bet (3) → 4-Bet (4). The 4-Bet is the most powerful weapon preflop, representing extremely strong hands or carefully designed bluffs.
Two types of 4-Bets: value 4-Bet (AA/KK/QQ/AKs — always 4-bet) and 4-Bet Bluff (A5s/A4s/A3s — A blocker + postflop playability).
Standard 4-Bet size: 2.2-2.5x the 3-Bet. Example: Open 2.5BB → 3-Bet 7.5BB → 4-Bet 16-19BB. IP can go slightly smaller (2.2x), OOP slightly bigger (2.5x).
Decision framework facing a 4-Bet: 1) 5-Bet All-in: AA/KK (always shove) 2) Call: QQ/AKs (strong but not unbeatable) 3) Fold: fold medium hands against a tight 4-Bet range.

Think ahead before 4-Betting: if opponent 5-Bet All-ins, what do I do? 4-Betting without a plan is the start of disaster. Use a linear 4-Bet range (strong hands only) at low stakes, add bluffs at higher stakes.

4Bet break-even analysis:
Required fold rate for a 4Bet bluff = 4Bet amount ÷ (pot + 4Bet amount)
Example: you 3Bet to 7.5BB, opponent 4Bets to 18BB
Required fold rate = 18 ÷ (7.5+18) ≈ 70.6%

Meaning: 70.6% is the fold rate your opponent needs for a 4Bet bluff to break even — fold more often than that and their bluff turns from zero EV into positive EV. So your own fold rate must stay below 70.6%, i.e. continue (3Bet or call) at least about 29.4% of the time.

Theory reference: range construction and game-theory principles in 4Bet spots are in Theory Academy T4 Chapter 1 "Range Thinking: From Single Hands to Probability Distributions". Preflop range filtering is closely tied to responses to a 4-Bet.

Counter-intuitive: a 4Bet Bluff needs an extremely high opponent fold rate (about 70%) to break even. That means it's not a strategy you can use frequently — it only works in specific spots (when opponents fold too much).
l2-squeeze: A Squeeze is a 3-Bet against 1 Open + 1 or more Calls. "Squeeze" vividly describes the middle player squeezed between the Opener and the Caller(s).

The value of Squeezing: 1) lots of dead money (the Open + Call chips are already in the pot) 2) high fold rate (Callers have weak ranges and often fold to 3-Bets) 3) isolating the Opener (heads-up in position).
Squeeze range (polarized): value hands (AA/KK/QQ/AKs/AQs) + Bluffs (A5s/A4s/A3s etc. Ax blockers). Size: 4-5x the Open (e.g. Open 2.5BB → Squeeze 10-12BB), plus 1x for each additional Caller.
Defending against a Squeeze: 1) 4-Bet: AA/KK 2) Call: strong but not premium (QQ/AKs) 3) Fold: weak call range (small pairs/suited connectors fold to a big Squeeze).
Best Squeeze timing: the Opener's range is wide (CO/BTN) + the Caller is a weak player (won't 4-Bet bluff). Avoid Squeeze bluffing against a tight UTG Open.
l2-bb-defense: The big blind (BB) has already posted 1BB, so facing an Open it only needs to top up the difference to call. Example: Open 2.5BB → BB needs only 1.5BB to call. This gives the BB excellent pot odds — defend with a wider range.

BB defense width in relative terms: widest against a BTN Open, then CO, tighter vs HJ, tightest vs UTG. The earlier the opponent opens, the tighter your defense should be; the exact composition is defined by the Range Trainer module and the GTO strategy chart.

Call: hands with postflop potential but not suited to 3-Betting (suited connectors/small pairs/wide suited hands). 3-Bet: polarized range — strong value (AA/KK/QQ/AKs) + Bluffs (A5s/A4s etc. Ax blockers).
Blind Defense Frequency: if you defend < 40%, opponents can profitably steal any time. If > 60%, over-defense gets punished by value bets. Adjust based on the opponent's Open range.
Defend tight against tight opponents (NIT/UTG Open), defend wide against loose opponents (LAG/BTN Open). The wider the opponent's Open range, the wider your defense should be.
l2-blind-war: Why Is the Blind War the Highest-Frequency Battle?
In 6-max, SB vs BB is the most frequent confrontation. When everyone before folds, the small blind faces a choice: compete or give up half a blind?
The SB's open range is in the same tier as the BTN (about 35%), because it only needs to beat one opponent. The BB can defend very wide against the SB, having posted 1BB against a weaker range.

Modern strategy uses a pure raise-or-fold approach from the SB (no limping):
• Open raise size: 2.5-3BB (bigger, since there's no positional advantage)
• Range: a very wide tier, about 35% of hands
• Includes all strong hands + many medium hands + some suited weak hands (as bluffs)

The BB should defend a wide range against the SB's Open:
• 3-Bet: only a small slice of the defense range (value hands + light 3-Bet bluffs)
• Call: the bulk of the defense range (many medium-strength hands)
• Fold: only the weakest hands
Positional disadvantage (the SB acts first postflop) is the key factor in the blind war. The SB should choose hands it can "play strongly", not "marginal hands".
If the opponent in the BB folds to 3-Bets a lot, tighten the SB open range slightly, but keep enough strong hands for 4-Bet bluffs.
l2-short-stack: When the effective stack is 20-50BB, strategy is completely different from 100BB deep stacks. The shallower the stack, the fewer postflop decisions and the more important preflop decisions become.
Core principle: the shallower the stack, the less important hand "playability" and the more important "raw equity". Suited connectors lose value while big cards gain value.

When the stack is ≤ 20BB, most situations offer only two choices:
• All-In (Push): the hand is strong enough
• Fold: the hand isn't strong enough

Push-range considerations:
1. Position (wider from late position)
2. Remaining stack (the difference between 15BB and 20BB is big)
3. How many players are left to act

At 30-50BB:
• Reduce the Open raise size to 2-2.2BB
• 3-Bets move toward a "raise/shove" mode
• Avoid calling with small suited connectors (not enough implied odds)
• Increase the share of big pairs and big cards
The most common short-stack mistake is using 100BB thinking. For example, calling a 3-Bet with 98s at 35BB is a big error — the set-mining realizability is too low.
In tournaments your stack constantly changes; switching strategy across stack depths is an essential skill.

l2-raise-q1.question: What is the standard preflop raise size in 6-max?
l2-raise-q1.explanation: The standard preflop raise is 2.5BB — the mainstream size in modern online poker.

l2-raise-q2.question: Why should you raise a uniform size?
l2-raise-q2.explanation: A uniform raise size hides your hand strength and stops opponents from reading your hand from your bet sizing.

l2-raise-q3.question: How does raise size affect the opponent's call rate?
l2-raise-q3.explanation: The bigger the raise, the weaker the calling hands and the lower the call rate — but the pot also grows.

l2-raise-q4.question: How should raise size vary by position?
l2-raise-q4.explanation: Modern strategy recommends a uniform raise size regardless of position — it hides hand strength.

l2-raise-q5.question: What is the main purpose of the standard 2.5BB raise?
l2-raise-q5.explanation: 2.5BB balances risk and reward: big enough to fold weak hands, small enough not to risk too much.

l2-3bet-q1.question: What does the "3" in 3-Bet represent?
l2-3bet-q1.explanation: The "3" means it's the 3rd preflop betting action: blinds(1) → open(2) → re-raise(3).

l2-3bet-q2.question: What type of 3-Bet range should beginners use?
l2-3bet-q2.explanation: Beginners should start with a linear range (3-Betting only strong hands), then learn the polarized range.

l2-3bet-q3.question: Which is NOT a purpose of 3-Betting?
l2-3bet-q3.explanation: 3-Betting is for value, fold equity, initiative, and isolation. Saving chips is not a purpose.

l2-3bet-q4.question: Against a UTG open, which hand is best to 3-Bet?
l2-3bet-q4.explanation: AA is the strongest starting hand — 3-Bet for value against any open.

l2-3bet-q5.question: How big is a standard 3-Bet relative to the original raise?
l2-3bet-q5.explanation: The standard 3-Bet is about 3x the original raise — e.g. 3-Bet to 7.5BB against a 2.5BB open.

l2-4bet-q1.question: Which hand is best as a 4-Bet Bluff?
l2-4bet-q1.explanation: A5s has an A blocker (reducing the odds of AA/AK) plus postflop playability (flush/straight potential) — the classic 4-Bet Bluff hand.

l2-4bet-q2.question: How big is a standard 4-Bet relative to the 3-Bet?

l2-4bet-q3.question: Facing a TAG's 4-Bet with JJ, what should you do?
options: Call or Fold depending on the situation
l2-4bet-q3.explanation: With JJ vs a TAG 4-Bet: if the TAG's range is tight (AA/KK/AKs) → Fold; if it contains bluffs → Call. No absolute answer — you need to read the opponent.

l2-4bet-q4.question: Facing a tight player's 4-Bet, which hand should you fold?
l2-4bet-q4.explanation: QQ can fold against a tight player's 4-Bet, since tight players mostly have AA/KK. But call against a wide-range player.

l2-4bet-q5.question: What is the main advantage of a 4-Bet Bluff?
options: The A blocker lowers the odds of opponent strong hands
l2-4bet-q5.explanation: 4-Bet Bluff hands usually have an A blocker, reducing the opponent's chance of AA/AK and increasing fold equity.

l2-squeeze-q1.question: What is a Squeeze Play?
l2-squeeze-q1.explanation: A Squeeze specifically means 3-Betting against 1 Open + 1 or more Calls, profiting from dead money and fold equity.

l2-squeeze-q2.question: After an Open 2.5BB + 1 Call, what's the standard Squeeze size?
l2-squeeze-q2.explanation: A Squeeze is usually 4-5x the Open, increasing with Callers. 2.5BB Open → 10-12BB Squeeze.

l2-squeeze-q3.question: Which hand is best as a Squeeze Bluff?
l2-squeeze-q3.explanation: A4s has an A blocker + postflop playability (flush/straight potential) — the classic Squeeze bluff hand.

l2-squeeze-q4.question: What is the best time to Squeeze?
l2-squeeze-q4.explanation: BTN has a wide Open range + weak Caller ranges, so the Squeeze fold rate is highest. Avoid Squeeze bluffing a tight UTG Open.

l2-squeeze-q5.question: Facing a Squeeze, which hand should 4-Bet?
l2-squeeze-q5.explanation: AA is the core 4-Bet hand — 4-Bet for value against a Squeeze. Don't slowplay AA.

l2-bb-q1.question: Facing a BTN Open to 2.5BB, which defense tier should the BB use?
options: Widest tier, including many medium-strength hands
l2-bb-q1.explanation: The BTN is the widest opening position at a 6-max table, and the BB has already posted 1BB with excellent odds to top up — so this is the widest defense tier of all positions.

l2-bb-q2.question: Facing an Open to 2.5BB, how much does the BB need to top up to call?
l2-bb-q2.explanation: The BB has 1BB invested, so against a 2.5BB Open it only needs 1.5BB to call — excellent pot odds.

l2-bb-q3.question: Facing a UTG Open, which defense tier should the BB use?
l2-bb-q3.explanation: UTG opens only the very strongest slice of hands, so the BB should defend its tightest range here, mostly with strong hands.

l2-bb-q4.question: In the BB, which hand suits a 3-Bet bluff?
l2-bb-q4.explanation: A4s has an A blocker that lowers the odds of AA/AK — the classic 3-Bet bluff hand.

l2-bb-q5.question: Compared with other opening positions, how should the BB's defense vs a BTN Open rank?
options: As tight as vs a UTG open
Tighter than vs a CO open
l2-bb-q5.explanation: The BTN opens the widest and the BB has 1BB invested with good odds, so its defense vs the BTN is the widest of all positions.

l2-blind-q1.question: Heads-up SB vs BB, which tier is the SB's standard open range?
options: As tight as an early-position open
l2-blind-q1.explanation: The SB only needs to beat one opponent, so its opening belongs to a very wide tier (about 35%); the exact composition is defined by the Range Trainer module and the GTO strategy chart.

l2-blind-q2.question: How wide should the BB's defense range be against an SB Open?
options: As tight as vs a BTN Open
l2-blind-q2.explanation: The BB has 1BB invested and the SB's range is weak, so the defense should be very wide (3-Bet + Call combined).

l2-blind-q3.question: What is the standard SB Open size?
l2-blind-q3.explanation: The SB lacks postflop position, so it uses a bigger size (2.5-3BB) to reduce the BB's defense frequency.

l2-blind-q4.question: What strategy should the SB use when opening?
l2-blind-q4.explanation: The SB should use a raise-or-fold strategy, avoiding limps. Limping gives the BB a free flop and loses initiative.

l2-blind-q5.question: Where does the SB's positional disadvantage show in the blind war?
l2-blind-q5.explanation: The SB acts first postflop (OOP) without information advantage — the core challenge of the blind war.

l2-short-q1.question: What strategy should you use at ≤20BB?
l2-short-q1.explanation: Below 20BB the strategy simplifies to Push or Fold — there's no middle ground.

l2-short-q2.question: Which hand type loses the most value when short-stacked?
l2-short-q2.explanation: The shallower the stack, the less the suited connectors' "playability" advantage works, and their low raw equity shows more.

l2-short-q3.question: How should the Open size adjust at 30-50BB?
l2-short-q3.explanation: Shallower stacks call for a smaller Open size of 2-2.2BB, lowering risk while keeping postflop maneuver room.

l2-short-q4.question: Which hand gains the most value when short-stacked?
l2-short-q4.explanation: The shallower the stack, the more the big pairs' raw equity advantage shows. Suited connectors' playability can't work.

l2-short-q5.question: How wide should the BTN push at 20BB?
l2-short-q5.explanation: At 20BB the BTN push range is about 30-40%, including all big pairs, big cards, and some suited connectors.

l2-raise-ex1.title: Uniform raise size: AA vs 76s
reasoning: AA is the strongest starting hand, but the raise size should be the standard 2.5BB
Don't raise bigger just because you have a strong hand (e.g. 4BB)
A uniform size stops opponents from reading information from your bet amount
2.5BB is enough to build the pot and get value
l2-raise-ex1.mistakeReasoning: Raising bigger with big hands is a classic tell. Opponents quickly learn big bet = strong hand, then fold — and you can't get value.

l2-raise-ex2.title: The problem of raising too small: Min-Raise
reasoning: KQs on the BTN is a standard open — raise to 2.5BB
Don't min-raise (2BB), which gives opponents too good pot odds
2.5BB makes it more expensive for opponents to call with weak hands
A standard size maximizes your positional advantage
l2-raise-ex2.mistakeReasoning: A min-raise gives opponents too good a price and lets too many weak hands see the flop. Your positional advantage gets diluted and postflop becomes harder.

l2-3bet-ex1.title: Value 3-Bet: QQ facing a CO Open
reasoning: QQ is a premium hand — 3-Bet for value against a CO open
3-Bet to 7.5BB (3x the original raise) is the standard size
Build a big pot to set up a postflop shove
The CO opens a wide range — QQ is way ahead
l2-3bet-ex1.mistakeReasoning: Flatting QQ is too passive. This hand is strong enough for a value 3-Bet; flatting brings more players in and lowers QQ's win rate.

l2-3bet-ex2.title: When NOT to 3-Bet: medium-strength hands
reasoning: KJs against a UTG open should Call, not 3-Bet
The UTG opening range is strong (early position) — KJs isn't strong enough for a value 3-Bet
A 3-Bet gets called or 4-Bet by the strong UTG range, putting you in a tough spot
Calling keeps the pot manageable and uses position postflop
l2-3bet-ex2.mistakeReasoning: 3-Betting KJs against a strong UTG range is -EV. When called you're usually behind; when 4-Bet you can only fold.

l2-4bet-ex1.title: Value 4-Bet defense: AKs facing a 3-Bet
reasoning: AKs should Call a LAG's 4-Bet — the LAG range is wide (AA/KK/QQ/AKs + bluffs)
AKs has about 40% equity against the LAG's 4-Bet range; calling keeps the pot manageable
5-Bet All-in is also acceptable, but calling lets the LAG keep bluffing
Use positional advantage postflop
l2-4bet-ex1.mistakeReasoning: Folding AKs to a LAG 4-Bet is too tight. The LAG's range is wide and AKs has enough equity to continue.

l2-4bet-ex2.title: Continuing bluff: C-Bet after 3-Betting
reasoning: Flop Kh8d3c, CO checks
Your preflop 3-Bet represents a strong range (AK/QQ/AKs) — C-Bet keeps the pressure on
TAG folds to postflop C-Bets after 3-Betting at a high rate (about 55%)
Even when called, A5 has backdoor flush + gutshot potential
l2-4bet-ex2.mistakeReasoning: Not C-Betting after a preflop 3-Bet is too passive and forfeits fold equity. The TAG folds a lot — keep pressuring.

l2-squeeze-ex1.title: Value Squeeze: QQ facing an Open + Call
reasoning: QQ is a premium hand — Squeeze for value against an Open + Call
There's already 6.5BB of dead money in the pot — a Squeeze can win it directly
MP and CO fold a lot to Squeezes
Even when called, QQ has good equity against both ranges
l2-squeeze-ex1.mistakeReasoning: Flatting QQ is too passive and lets SB/BB see the flop cheaply. A Squeeze collects dead money + fold equity.

l2-squeeze-ex2.title: Squeeze Bluff: A5s facing a wide Open + Call
reasoning: The CO opens wide + the SB calls weak — the Squeeze fold rate is high
A5s has an A blocker, lowering the odds of AA/AK
The 6BB dead money is worth competing for
When called, there's flush/straight potential to play postflop
l2-squeeze-ex2.mistakeReasoning: Flatting A5s makes the pot multiway and lowers equity. A Squeeze profits directly from fold equity.

l2-bb-ex1.title: Wide BB defense: K9s facing a BTN Open
reasoning: K9s should Call and defend against a BTN Open
The BTN is the widest opening position at a 6-max table — K9s has enough equity
Only 1.5BB to top up — excellent pot odds (about 2.5:1)
Suited high cards have postflop potential (top pair/flush)
l2-bb-ex1.mistakeReasoning: Folding K9s to a BTN Open is too tight. The BTN range is wide and the BB has good odds — defend wide.

l2-bb-ex2.title: BB 3-Bet: A5s facing a CO Open
reasoning: A5s suits a 3-Bet bluff against a CO Open
The A blocker lowers the odds of AA/AK
TAG folds to 3-Bets at a high rate (about 55%)
When called, there's flush/straight potential postflop
l2-bb-ex2.mistakeReasoning: Calling A5s is OK but passive. A 3-Bet gains fold equity + initiative — more +EV.
